  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section contains the opening header of the maamar for Shabbos Haazinu, 13 Tishrei 5722.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">B'Siyata Dishmaya.</t>
    <t s="1">Shabbos Parshas Haazinu,</t>
    <t s="2">13 Tishrei*,</t>
    <t s="3">5722</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section notes that the maamar is an uncorrected draft.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">(Uncorrected draft)</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the verse "Like an eagle stirring its nest...", linking it to guarding Israel as the pupil of God's eye, and the superiority of Israel over angels.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"Like an eagle stirring its nest, hovering over its young, He spreads His wings, takes it, bears it on His pinions. God alone leads him..."</t>
    <t s="1">And this refers to what is stated earlier,</t>
    <t s="2">"He guards him as the pupil of His eye."</t>
    <t s="3">That through this—that He guards him as the pupil of His eye—through this, "like an eagle stirring its nest,"</t>
    <t s="4">and therefore, "He spreads His wings, takes it, bears it on His pinions. God alone leads him."</t>
    <t s="5">And the explanation of "He guards him as the pupil of His eye":</t>
    <t s="6">It is known</t>
    <t s="7">that there are Sefiros and angels that are called by the name "eyes,"</t>
    <t s="8">and as explained in Torah Ohr</t>
    <t s="9">regarding the matter of "the eyes of God roaming and roving," which are two types among the angels.</t>
    <t s="10">However, Israel, who are innermost relative to the ministering angels, are the aspect of the "pupil of His eye."</t>
    <t s="11">For the eye, although it is a vessel for the power of sight,</t>
    <t s="12">nevertheless, the essence of sight is from the pupil within the eye.</t>
    <t s="13">And this is the superiority of Israel over the angels:</t>
    <t s="14">that the angels are called by the name "eyes" in general,</t>
    <t s="15">and Israel are the aspect of the "pupil of His eye."</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
